findings.claim: The evaluator never clamps the instance frame of a shot's own range: it throws past the end, and passes the real frame to the overrides and to the rig and reveal layers. The integrity rule makes the instance grow so that it never does.

`heldInstance` exists only at the tip, in `resolveShotAtOffset`: it clamps to `[0, instance.durationFrames - 1]` and is true only when that moved the frame; its reader is the other deck of a transition, and inside the range it equals `resolveShotAtEditFrame`.
The channels: `cycle` continues with a modulo of the instance frame (not held); `event` holds its final value by design; the baked rig pose and the reveal hold past the end of their own track.

d07_audit.for_q2: The plan's D07 behaviour (new frames evaluated as real: `cycle` continues, `event` holds its final value) is what the origin does, so it is NOT a divergence and Q2 is not triggered: the owner has no decision to take. Caveats: decision #6 says 'the runtime holds the last frame ... heldInstance', which reads like a hold of the whole instance; the code does not do that, and the pilot code of #6 (`shots/`) is not in the clone (ORIGIN_NOT_EXECUTED), so the reading is from the text and the code around it. The reference does not evaluate frames: D07 changes no case of the corpus.
d07_audit.question: Frames added by the growth of an instance (#6): held or evaluated as real?
d07_audit.summary: The frames of an instance grown by #6 are evaluated as real frames of a longer instance. `heldInstance` is not what holds them: it is set only for the OTHER deck of an effects transition, when the wanted instance frame falls outside `[0, durationFrames - 1]` of the (already grown) instance; and inside the shot's own range `resolveShotAtOffset` answers what `resolveShotAtEditFrame` answers. What 'holds' in decision #6 are the channels that hold by themselves (event channels with `holdFinal`, the baked rig pose, the reveal); a `cycle` channel keeps cycling.

oracle_choices.AUDIO_WARNING: `explain` compares the edit with the END of the audio window and allows one frame of slack; `locked` is the `editLocked` flag of the instance; `NARRATION_PAST_EDIT` is not modelled.
oracle_choices.AUTO_RESERVE: Decision #29 writes `a = min(d, instanceStartFrame, cameraInFrame)` minus the transition reserve. The oracle reads it as `a = max(0, min(d, min(instanceStartFrame, cameraInFrame) - reserve))` (the reserve is taken out of the head frames that EXIST, so a short slip is still fully anchored). The literal reading is `max(0, min(d, instanceStartFrame, cameraInFrame) - reserve)`. The two differ when `d` is smaller than the head frames: the corpus has a case tagged AUTO_RESERVE that shows it, and the coordinator should settle it before S1 (no pilot code to execute).
oracle_choices.BOUNDARY: A point (a key) at the frame where frames are inserted moves with them (`frame >= at`), and a clip that starts there moves whole; a clip that ENDS there (exclusive end) does not stretch. For a removed stretch [a, b): a point inside is dropped, a point at or after `b` moves back by `b - a`. The origin documents say 'after the point' and 'inside the removed stretch' without the border.
oracle_choices.CHAIN_MIDDLE: A clip that CONTAINS the removed stretch keeps its keys at the same clip-relative frames (#12 'not re-timed'), pruned at the new end; a clip whose HEAD is cut shifts its keys by the cut (instants kept), pruned below 0 (D09).
oracle_choices.EMPTY_CONTAINER: When the last key track of a light is removed, its `keys` object is removed too (the list rule of #15 says 'undefined'; the container is not mentioned).
oracle_choices.GATE: Findings of the final gate are reported as CANDIDATE_REJECTED with the codes of the origin rules the candidate breaks (integrity, joins, fx clips and keys, transitions); the pose check of continuous joins (CONTINUOUS_*_JUMP) and the lighting reader are not modelled (T06).
oracle_choices.LOCKED_AUTO: `auto` that would follow tries to stay anchored when `editLocked` forbids following (#10, #30); if anchoring is not possible either (not enough head), the op is LOCKED.
oracle_choices.REFUSAL_ORDER: When two rules refuse the same op the oracle reports, in order: SHOTS_OPTION_NOT_YET, SHOT_NOT_FOUND, SHOTS_NOT_ADJACENT, SHOTS_LAYER_NOT_YET, SHOT_TOO_SHORT, CONTINUOUS_JOIN, NO_HEAD_FRAMES, EDIT_TOO_LONG, LOCKED, TRANSITION_TOO_LONG, then the gate (CANDIDATE_REJECTED). The corpus has one rule per refusal case.
oracle_choices.TRANSITION_KEYS: Transitions in the minimal document have no keys; `shrink_transitions` only changes `durationFrames`.
